sections.h2: Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh hold about 66% of stray cattle

chart.title: Three states hold 33.1 lakh of the country's 50.2 lakh stray cattle
chart.sub: Stray cattle by state, top ten, lakh animals (20th Livestock Census, 2019).

sections.means: The ten states in the chart hold 90% of the country's stray cattle, so the problem is concentrated rather than spread evenly.
sections.todo: Target the states that hold most of the stray cattle first when planning collection and shelter capacity.

sections.h2: Plastic in cows' stomachs runs to tens of kilograms in single cases

chart.title: Single cows in vet reports carried 48 to 71 kg of plastic
chart.sub: Plastic removed from stomachs in case reports and hospital studies, kg.
chart.source: Indian veterinary case reports and hospital studies, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Plastic in the rumen knots into a mass that fills the space food should take, so the animal eats less, loses weight and gives less milk.
sections.todo: Keep plastic out of cows by separating wet waste, collecting it daily in closed vehicles and keeping animals away from collection points.

sections.h2: Chemical-pulp paper is far more digestible to cattle than newsprint

chart.title: Paper made from chemical pulp is up to 98% digestible, against about 30% for newsprint
chart.sub: Digestibility of paper in cattle feed, %.

sections.means: Plain paper made from chemical pulp, such as kraft and bagasse, is the most digestible option, though it softens when wet.
sections.todo: Test whether bagasse or kraft paper bags last a day of wet kitchen waste without tearing before using them widely.
